thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for model rwd-gpt-7b-stream (us-west-2). p95 ~1.1s -> 3.2s, p99 ~0.9s -> 9.3s over the last 5m. SLO breach detected. correlated errors: streaming stalls, tail decode timeouts. ticket INC-4921 created.

alex: I'm on it. seeing the same in Grafana (streaming response times jump around 22:14 PDT). tagging eng-runtime.

jamie: Oncall-SRE joining. Do we have a recent deploy? any kernel/build changes in the last 6h?

deploy-bot: deploy:build-2026-03-12-trt8-9df7 was rolled to us-west-2 at 18:47 UTC. Flags: --enable-flashattn --compiler-flags="-O3 -march=native -funroll-loops".

tim: that's the new TRT8/FlashAttention build. We rolled thumbnails of the decode kernel for latency perf. Could be a regression with large sequence streams (streaming stalls -> paging).

maria: quick check: memory/cgroup metrics show increased host GPU memory pressure + occasional paging events around the same window. not full OOM but lots of stalls in nvml. Logs show repeated kernel launch times spiking.

alex: can someone run a quick p99 breakdown by model and instance type? I want to know if it's localized to particular GPU SKU or all nodes.

jamie: running query now. results: p99 spike concentrated on gtx-a100-80g nodes in pool-usw2-stream-01. other pools relatively stable.

liz: customer-ops: we've seen 3 customers report streaming timeouts in the last 10m (support tickets linked in INC-4921). prepping a short note. pls confirm ETA for mitigation.

tim: probable root: new FlashAttention kernel combined with compiler flags produced a corner case that increases tail latency when KV cache gets larger and we hit a kernel recompile path. There's also evidence of increased host->device memory copies when the kernel falls back.

maria: stack snippet from worker logs:

```
2026-03-12T18:48:23Z worker[pid=4421]: decode: kernel_launch_time=84ms seq_len=1024 model=rwd-gpt-7b-stream
2026-03-12T18:48:24Z worker[pid=4421]: nvlink_copy: 120ms -> fallback memcpy, paging_event=1
2026-03-12T18:48:24Z worker[pid=4421]: decode: tail_latency=5.2s, flush_kv_cache=true
```

alex: thanks. immediate mitigation options? rollback build, disable flashattn runtime flag, or route streaming traffic off the affected pool. Which is fastest?

tim: fastest is to switch routing for streaming model to the dedicated pool with legacy kernels (pool-usw2-legacy-02). I can flip routing in the control plane in ~2m. rollback build will take longer and needs coordination.

jamie: I can hot-toggle runtime config to disable flashattn on the pool but that requires draining and restart of workers (5-7m). routing flip is less risky.

alex: do it. tim flip routing. jamie prepare the disable-flag plan as follow-up. liz hold on the customer note and mark in-progress.

tim: executing routing change:

```bash
# route streaming model to legacy pool
api call: POST /v1/routing/update 
{ "model": "rwd-gpt-7b-stream", "from_pool": "pool-usw2-stream-01", "to_pool": "pool-usw2-legacy-02", "drain": false }
```

deploy-bot: routing update accepted (req-43502). draining=false, immediate traffic shift.

maria: metrics after switch (1m): p95 back to ~1.3s, p99 down to ~1.9s. streaming stalls drop significantly. looks effective.

alex: good. jamie, can you escalate a rollback of build-2026-03-12-trt8-9df7 for non-streaming workloads or do a narrower patch to the decode kernel? We need a root cause fix, not just route workaround.

jamie: creating task: RUNTIME-1208 to bisect the build and isolate the FlashAttention kernel path. will try replicating locally with long-seq workloads to reproduce. planning window 2h.

tim: notes for reproduction: sequence length 1024-2048, continuous streaming with KV growth, run with sampler stress and set --compiler-flags to match prod. suspicious area: compilepath fallback that triggers CPU memcpy path on certain GPU driver versions.

maria: adding logs + kernel traces to the ticket. I've attached nvprof trace snippets and the worker crash logs.

liz: customer update: sending a short message acknowledging latency issue, mitigation in place (traffic shifted), engineers investigating, next update in 60m.

alex: handoff to next oncall (overnight): jamie/tim will pick this up. jamie please summarize action items in the ticket.

jamie: Handoff summary:
- mitigation: traffic routed to pool-usw2-legacy-02 (complete)
- rollback: under consideration, RUNTIME-1208 created for bisect
- follow-ups: (1) reproduce and fix compilepath regression (tim), (2) optional patch to make FlashAttention compile fallback less punitive (maria), (3) run canary with small percent on legacy pool after fix (alex)
- customer impact: 3 reported timeouts, no data loss, SLO breach recorded for p99 window.

tim: I'll attempt a minimal reproducer and open a PR to guard the compilepath. aiming for patch in next 4-6h.

alex: thanks all. liz send the 60m update. jamie/tim you own the overnight. I'll close the immediate pager when handoff done. :white_check_mark:

liz: posted update to affected customers and internal ops channel. linking messages in INC-4921.

alex: closing pager now, handing to eng-runtime oncall. next update at 60m or earlier if regression found.

incident-bot: pager_status: acknowledged by alex, routed to eng-runtime.

deploy-bot: note: build-2026-03-12-trt8-9df7 will be removed from rollout list pending RUNTIME-1208 investigation.

maria: leaving traces and a small playbook in the ticket for future incidents (how to route quickly + runtime flags to toggle).

jamie: oncall-handoff to @eng-runtime-night: please monitor p95/p99 for rwd-gpt-7b-stream and watch for regressions when rolling any new kernel builds. attach me if you need escalation.

alex: good handoff. thanks team.
